chunks: And it was narrated from Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbbād al-Makkī that he said: I heard Sufyān al-Thawrī asking Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about al-takhḍīr.

So he said: “A man from the Anṣār died, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was informed of his death. He said to those among his relatives who were responsible for him: ‘Place greenery on your companion. How few are those made green on the Day of Resurrection.’”
He said: And what is al-takhḍīr? He said: “A green palm branch is placed from the base of the hands to the base of the collarbone.”

key_terms.التَّخْضِيرِ: placing greenery, specifically a green branch, with the deceased
key_terms.الْأَنْصَارِ: the Anṣār, the Helpers from Madinah
key_terms.الْمُخَضَّرِينَ: those made green or adorned with greenery
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about placing a green branch with the deceased?
ai.summary: This hadith reports Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام explaining the practice of al-takhḍīr for the deceased through a report from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It describes placing a green palm branch on the deceased and links this act with the Day of Resurrection, indicating its significance in funerary practice.
